content:
Sam: Quick brain-dump — thinking about a "fast-path" for data-sovereignty tenants so writes can be accepted locally even when the region isn't the canonical primary. Goal: reduce tail latency for EU/DE customers and avoid cross-border egress when possible.

Priya: Curious about legal surface — if we accept local write and replicate later, do we violate any residency guarantees? Need clarity from legal but from product side some customers asked for local-first with explicit eventual-consistency promises.

Marco: Architecturally this could be a control-plane shim + per-tenant policy. Runtime would put write into local escrow, respond with local ack, and async-replicate to primary. We mark those keys with `scope: escrowed` and attach a `consistency: eventual-local` header.

Lina: Operational concerns: how do we handle failover/rollbacks? If primary rejects or conflict arises, we need a deterministic reconciliation and a way to surface conflicts to the owner. Also think about retention of escrowed entries during region outage.

Priya: Good point. Requirements I'd propose: 1) explicit billing/contract flag per tenant, 2) audit trail for escrowed writes, 3) opt-in only, no silent fallback, 4) SLOs documented (e.g., replication target < 30s typical, 5 mins worst-case).

Sam: Agree. Also want to avoid changing app-level semantics widely. We should offer two modes: `local-fast-path` (local ack + async replicate) and `local-strong-proxy` (proxy to primary synchronously when available). Apps choose.

Marco: Implementation sketch:
```
policy:
  tenant_id: T-1234
  mode: local-fast-path
  ack_level: local
  replication: async -> primary
  conflict_resolution: last-writer-wins|merge-hook
```
We'd add a `region-handled` header to traces and metric plumbing.

Lina: For operator tooling: need an operator command to surface escrow backlog per-tenant, and an automated drain/flush job with backpressure detection. Also alerting if backlog > X or replication latency > SLA.

Priya: How to communicate semantics to customers? We should update the API docs and create a short contract clause: "writes accepted locally are propagated to canonical storage asynchronously; eventual consistency guarantees apply." Also include recommended patterns for idempotency and conflict handling.

Sam: Thought: we can reuse existing KV lease token for ownership hints to avoid changing data model much. When a tenant toggles fast-path we flip a routing flag in the control plane and emit a config change event.

Marco: Race conditions: concurrent writes from two regions for same tenant while in transition. Proposal: disallow toggling mode while there is non-zero escrow backlog (atomic toggle guarded by drain). Also sequence numbers on escrow items to aid reconciliation.

Lina: Test matrix: small canary with 2 tenants EU-only, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, escrow backlog growth under 10% traffic surge, and failure injection (primary partition) to validate replay. Ops runbook link: <https://wiki/redwood/ops/escrow-drain-playbook> (draft).

ops-bot: Deploy checklist created: https://deploys.redwood/escrow-fastpath/checklist — runbook step 3 needs an owner.

Sam: Next actions: Marco to prototype control-plane flag + telemetry in a branch, Lina to draft operator runbook, Priya to coordinate legal/product notes and customer comms. I'll pair with Marco on the prototype API for `mode` toggle.

Priya: I'll ping Legal today and loop in Solutions to line up a pilot customer.

Marco: I'll open a small spike PR with a runtime shim and synthetic replay tests. ETA EOW.

Lina: I'll start the runbook skeleton and add required alert thresholds.

Sam: Cool — let's reconvene next Tue after spikes. 

Priya: +1 :thumbsup:

Marco: +1

Lina: :white_check_mark:
